speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing intense itching and developing red bumps on your thigh and other body parts; can you describe exactly how these bumps look and if they are itchy or painful?

How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any recent travel, new medications, insect bites, or contact with plants or animals?

Do you have anyone else in your household experiencing similar symptoms, or have you been in areas with known insect infestations recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies infestation.

The history of intense itching, red bumps, and a recent business trip to Miami (a common hotspot for scabies outbreaks) strongly points to this diagnosis. Given your medical history and current medications, could you confirm if anyone in your household or close contacts is experiencing similar itching or skin bumps? Additionally, have you noticed any burrows, which appear as tiny, wavy lines under the skin, particularly in the web spaces of your fingers or around your genitals?
